title: 人工智能，从零搭建 · 第11部分：一路下山

chapters.Outro: 回顾，以及这些想法会在哪里再现

decccc5e790a.en: Every model in this series is trained by walking downhill. But how you walk matters enormously. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here's part four's narrow valley again, and three walkers starting from the same place. <bookmark mark='b'/> Plain gradient descent zigzags across the valley. Momentum builds up speed along it. Adam rescales each direction separately, and heads almost straight for the bottom.
decccc5e790a.zh: 本系列的每一个模型，都是靠一路下山训练出来的。但怎么走，差别非常大。<bookmark mark='a'/>这又是第4部分那条狭窄的山谷，三个下山的人，从同一个地方出发。<bookmark mark='b'/>单纯的梯度下降，在山谷两壁之间来回折返。动量沿着山谷越走越快。Adam把每个方向分别重新缩放，几乎径直奔向谷底。

f3a37af7f2a8.en: This part is about the optimizers that train real models: why the noise of small batches helps, why training lives at the edge of instability, how Adam and the newer Muon reshape each step, <bookmark mark='a'/> and how the learning rate should change over a training run.
f3a37af7f2a8.zh: 这一部分讲的是训练真实模型的那些优化器：为什么小批量带来的噪声反而有帮助，为什么训练总在失稳的边缘徘徊，Adam和更新的Muon怎样重新塑造每一步，<bookmark mark='a'/>以及在一次训练过程中，学习率应该怎样变化。

8c99f196dd7d.en: Computing the exact gradient means going through all the training data, for every single step. Real models train on trillions of words; nobody can afford that. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here's a real loss with two weights: part six's logistic regression on two word rates. With the whole dataset, each step goes straight downhill. <bookmark mark='b'/> Instead, estimate the gradient from a small random batch. Sixteen pages: the path wobbles, but it's twenty-eight times cheaper per step. <bookmark mark='c'/> One page at a time: wild, but still it gets there.
8c99f196dd7d.zh: 要算出精确的梯度，每走一步，都得把全部训练数据过一遍。真实的模型要在几万亿个词上训练，这样做谁也负担不起。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是一个真实的损失，只有两个权重：第6部分的逻辑回归，用的是两个词频。用上整个数据集，每一步都径直朝下坡走。<bookmark mark='b'/>换个办法：随机抽一小批样本，用它们来估计梯度。用16页：路径摇摇晃晃，但每一步的代价只有原来的28分之1。<bookmark mark='c'/>一次只用1页：走得歪歪扭扭，但最后还是能走到。

2ad3b1395533.en: Keep going, and the walker never quite stops. It jiggles around the bottom forever, in a cloud. <bookmark mark='a'/> That's part five's stochastic differential equation: a push downhill, plus random kicks whose size grows with the learning rate and shrinks with the batch. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sixteen times the batch, and the cloud is about 4 times narrower: one over the square root of sixteen. <bookmark mark='c'/> The noise isn't only a cost. Picture a sharp minimum, a narrow pit, beside a wide one, a broad basin. A jiggling walker can't stay in the narrow pit, so it tends to settle where the valley is wide, and wide minima tend to work better on new data.
2ad3b1395533.zh: 一直走下去，它也永远不会真正停下来，而是在谷底附近没完没了地抖动，散成一团云。<bookmark mark='a'/>这正是第5部分的随机微分方程：一股往下坡的推力，加上随机的踢动；学习率越大，踢得越猛，批量越大，踢得越轻。<bookmark mark='b'/>批量变成16倍，这团云的宽度就缩小到大约4分之1：正是16的平方根分之1。<bookmark mark='c'/>噪声不只是代价。想象一个尖锐的极小值，一个狭窄的坑，旁边还有一个宽阔的极小值，一片开阔的盆地。不停抖动的它，在狭窄的坑里待不住，所以往往会停在山谷宽阔的地方，而宽的极小值，在新数据上往往表现更好。

f6f77fec6849.en: Chapter two. The edge of stability.

a5c64344e27b.en: Start with the simplest possible case: a bowl with curvature lambda, and a step of size eta. Each step multiplies the distance from the bottom by one minus eta times lambda. <bookmark mark='a'/> If that's between minus one and one, the steps shrink and settle. <bookmark mark='b'/> If eta times lambda is more than two, each step overshoots further than the last, and it blows up. So for a given step size, gradient descent can only live where the curvature is below two over eta.
a5c64344e27b.zh: 先从最简单的情形说起：一个曲率为λ的碗，步长为η。每走一步，到碗底的距离都要乘上1减去η乘以λ。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果这个数在负1和1之间，步子就会越来越小，最后稳定下来。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果η乘以λ大于2，每一步都比上一步冲得更远，最后彻底发散。所以，给定步长，梯度下降只能待在曲率小于η分之2的地方。

c01de8fb9e80.en: Now a real network: the spirals from part nine, trained with the full gradient at two step sizes. Track the sharpness, the Hessian's largest eigenvalue, from part four: how tightly the valley curves along its steepest direction, the lambda of that bowl. <bookmark mark='a'/> It climbs, and climbs, until it hits two over eta, and then it stays there, hovering at the edge, while the loss keeps going down. <bookmark mark='b'/> Double the step size, and the network settles at half the sharpness. Training doesn't avoid the edge of stability: it seeks it out. Cohen and colleagues found this in 2021, and nobody had expected it.
c01de8fb9e80.zh: 现在换成一个真实的网络：第9部分的那两条螺旋，用完整的梯度，分别以两种步长来训练。盯住它的锐度，也就是第4部分讲过的黑塞矩阵的最大特征值：山谷沿着最陡的方向弯得有多紧，也就是那个碗的λ。<bookmark mark='a'/>它一路往上爬，爬了又爬，直到碰上η分之2，然后就停在那里，悬在边缘上，而损失还在继续下降。<bookmark mark='b'/>步长加倍，网络就稳定在一半的锐度上。训练并没有躲开稳定性边缘：它是主动去找它的。2021年，科恩和同事们发现了这一点，在此之前，谁都没有料到。

315f624c62ec.en: Momentum keeps a running average of recent gradients, m, the direction they've been pointing lately, and steps along that; beta sets how long that memory lasts. Zigzags cancel; steady directions add up. <bookmark mark='a'/> Adam, from 2014, also tracks the average squared gradient for every weight, v, its typical size, and divides by its square root, plus a tiny epsilon so it never divides by zero. Each weight gets its own step size: large where the gradients are small, small where they're large. <bookmark mark='b'/> AdamW adds one fix: it shrinks the weights directly, separately from the gradient. That's the optimizer that trained most of today's language models.
315f624c62ec.zh: 动量记下最近那些梯度的滑动平均m，也就是它们最近一直指向的方向，然后沿着这个方向走；β决定这份记忆能保持多久。来回折返的部分互相抵消，方向稳定的部分不断累加。<bookmark mark='a'/>Adam是2014年提出的，它还为每一个权重记下梯度平方的平均v，也就是梯度通常有多大，再除以它的平方根，外加一个极小的ε，保证永远不会除以0。这样，每个权重都有了自己的步长：梯度小的地方，步子大；梯度大的地方，步子小。<bookmark mark='b'/>AdamW只多了一处修正：它直接把权重缩小，和梯度分开来做。今天的大多数语言模型，就是用这个优化器训练出来的。

945f32c560d8.en: Here they are on a real task: a small character model, like part nine's, trained on the books for two and a half thousand steps, each optimizer at a good learning rate. <bookmark mark='a'/> Plain SGD is slowest. Momentum helps. <bookmark mark='b'/> Adam and AdamW are far ahead after the same number of steps.
945f32c560d8.zh: 把它们放到一个真实的任务上：一个小型的字符模型，和第9部分的类似，在那些书上训练2500步，每个优化器都用一个合适的学习率。<bookmark mark='a'/>单纯的SGD最慢。加上动量，有所帮助。<bookmark mark='b'/>走了同样多的步数，Adam和AdamW遥遥领先。

50542f76c7e5.en: What does a number like that read like? Here both models continue the same few words, with the same random draws, at checkpoints during training. <bookmark mark='a'/> Before any training, every character of the books is equally likely: 7.5 bits each, and the text is noise from the whole alphabet. <bookmark mark='b'/> After 100 steps they have spaces, and short words like 'the', 'to' and 'and'. <bookmark mark='c'/> By step 1,000, most of what they write is word-shaped, and <bookmark mark='d'/> by the end, at about 2.6 bits, there's punctuation, a line break, even the start of dialogue. AdamW is ahead at every checkpoint. Since both draw the same random numbers, their texts rhyme; the difference is how far each one has come down the hill.
50542f76c7e5.zh: 这样一个数字，读起来是什么样？这里两个模型接着同样的几个词往下写，用同样的随机数，在训练途中的几个检查点上。<bookmark mark='a'/>训练开始之前，书里的每个字符都一样可能：每个7.5比特，写出来的是整个字母表里的噪声。<bookmark mark='b'/>训练100步之后，它们有了空格，还有the、to、and这样的短词。<bookmark mark='c'/>到第1000步，它们写出的大部分东西都像单词了，<bookmark mark='d'/>到最后，大约2.6比特的时候，有了标点、换行，甚至对话的开头。每个检查点上，AdamW都领先。因为两者抽到的是同样的随机数，它们写出的文字彼此押韵；区别只在于，各自在山坡上走下来了多远。

e175032fbf33.en: Adam treats every weight separately. But the weights of a layer form a matrix, and a matrix has structure: part three's singular values. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here's a real gradient matrix from the character model. A few directions dominate; most are tiny. A step along it mostly pushes the few big directions further. <bookmark mark='b'/> Muon, from 2024, takes the gradient's singular value decomposition and sets every singular value to one: the same push in every direction. <bookmark mark='c'/> It doesn't even compute the SVD. Five rounds of a matrix polynomial, Newton–Schulz, do it approximately and fast.
e175032fbf33.zh: Adam把每个权重分开对待。可是一层的权重组成一个矩阵，而矩阵是有结构的：也就是第3部分讲的奇异值。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是字符模型里一个真实的梯度矩阵。少数几个方向占了主导，大多数方向都微乎其微。沿着它走一步，主要是把那几个大方向推得更远。<bookmark mark='b'/>Muon是2024年提出的，它对梯度做奇异值分解，再把每个奇异值都设成1：每个方向都得到同样大小的推力。<bookmark mark='c'/>它甚至不用真的去算奇异值分解。一个矩阵多项式，叫作牛顿–舒尔茨迭代，迭代5轮，就能又快又近似地做到这一点。

c1be7e06141c.en: Why set the singular values to one? Because it's the steepest step under the right notion of size. <bookmark mark='p'/> Picture what a matrix does to a circle of directions. The gradient stretches it into a long, thin ellipse: a few directions dominate. <bookmark mark='q'/> Muon's step keeps it a circle: every direction moved by the same amount. <bookmark mark='a'/> Ask for the step that lowers the loss fastest, to first order, among all steps that stretch no direction by more than eta: a bound on the spectral norm, which is what matters for a matrix that multiplies vectors. <bookmark mark='b'/> Write the gradient in its singular directions. Each term can be pushed down by at most eta times its singular value. <bookmark mark='c'/> And one step achieves every bound at once: minus eta times U V transpose. If no direction may be stretched by more than eta, the best move pushes every direction by exactly eta. Adam, in the same sense, is the steepest step when each weight is bounded separately.
c1be7e06141c.zh: 为什么要把奇异值都设成1？因为在正确的“大小”概念下，这是最陡的一步。<bookmark mark='p'/>想象一个矩阵对一圈方向做了什么。梯度把这个圆拉成一个又长又细的椭圆：少数几个方向占了主导。<bookmark mark='q'/>Muon的这一步让它保持是个圆：每个方向都移动同样的量。<bookmark mark='a'/>在所有不把任何方向拉长超过η的步子里，找出一阶近似下让损失下降最快的那一步：这是对谱范数的约束，而对一个要去乘向量的矩阵来说，谱范数才是要紧的大小。<bookmark mark='b'/>把梯度写成它的奇异方向之和。每一项最多只能被压低η乘以它的奇异值。<bookmark mark='c'/>而有一步能同时达到所有这些界：负η乘以U乘V转置。如果任何方向都不许被拉长超过η，最好的走法就是把每个方向都正好推η。同样的意义上，Adam是在每个权重各自受限时最陡的那一步。

5407318c503c.en: How does Newton–Schulz do it without an SVD? Each round, X becomes a times X, plus b times X X transpose X, plus c times X X transpose squared X. On the singular values, that's just one polynomial, applied to each of them separately. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here it is, with Keller Jordan's coefficients. It rises steeply from zero, so small singular values grow fast, and it hovers around one. <bookmark mark='b'/> Follow one value: five rounds carry it up to about one. <bookmark mark='c'/> And here are all two hundred and fifty-six of our gradient's singular values, round by round. Every one above a hundredth of the largest, 104 of them, ends in a band between 0.68 and 1.13: not exactly one, but close enough, and the coefficients were tuned to get there in five rounds. The tiniest ones, mostly numerical dust, climb but don't arrive, which costs nothing.
5407318c503c.zh: 牛顿–舒尔茨迭代是怎么不用SVD就做到的？每一轮，X变成a乘X，加上b乘X X转置 X，再加上c乘X X转置的平方 X。落到奇异值上，这只是一个多项式，分别作用在每个奇异值上。<bookmark mark='a'/>这就是它，用的是Keller Jordan的系数。它从0开始陡峭地上升，所以小的奇异值长得很快，然后在1附近徘徊。<bookmark mark='b'/>跟着一个值走：5轮把它带到1左右。<bookmark mark='c'/>这是我们梯度的全部256个奇异值，一轮一轮地变化。凡是大于最大值百分之一的，一共104个，最后都落在0.68到1.13之间：不正好是1，但足够接近，而这些系数正是为了5轮就到这里而调出来的。最小的那些，大多是数值上的尘埃，会往上爬但到不了，这没有任何代价。

20d0f311ffe0.en: On the same character model, with Muon on the hidden matrices, the weight grids inside the network, and AdamW on the rest: the character table, the output layer and the small bias terms. <bookmark mark='a'/> it reaches 2.50 bits, ahead of AdamW's 2.61. Muon has since been scaled up: Moonshot AI reported that it needs about half the compute of AdamW, and used a version of it to train Kimi K2.
20d0f311ffe0.zh: 还是同一个字符模型，隐藏层的矩阵，也就是网络内部那些权重网格，用Muon；其余的用AdamW：字符表、输出层，还有那些小小的偏置项。<bookmark mark='a'/>它达到了2.50比特，领先于AdamW的2.61。此后，Muon被推广到了大得多的规模：月之暗面报告说，它只需要AdamW大约一半的算力，还用它的一个变体训练了Kimi K2。

431e2ad0276d.en: Scaled up, Muon hit one problem. <bookmark mark='h'/> In attention, which part thirteen builds, each word scores how relevant every earlier word is. A head is one such scorer, and its scores come from two weight matrices, the query and the key. In some heads the attention scores kept growing until training blew up. Moonshot's fix for Kimi K2 is QK-clip. <bookmark mark='a'/> After each step, look at each head's largest score. <bookmark mark='b'/> If it's above a threshold tau, shrink the two weight matrices that make it, that head's query and key weights, by the square root of tau over the score, each, so the score lands exactly on tau. Nothing else changes. <bookmark mark='c'/> With it, Kimi K2 trained on fifteen and a half trillion tokens without a single loss spike.
431e2ad0276d.zh: 规模一大，Muon碰到了一个问题。<bookmark mark='h'/>在注意力机制里，也就是第13部分要搭建的东西，每个词都要给前面每一个词打分，看它有多相关。一个注意力头就是这样一个打分器，它的分数来自两个权重矩阵：查询和键。有些注意力头的注意力分数一直变大，直到训练崩掉。月之暗面为Kimi K2给出的解决办法是QK-clip。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一步之后，看看每个头最大的那个分数。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果它超过阈值τ，就把产生这个分数的两个权重矩阵，也就是这个头的查询权重和键权重，各自乘上τ除以这个分数的平方根，让分数正好落在τ上。别的都不变。<bookmark mark='c'/>有了它，Kimi K2在15.5万亿个词元上训练，一次损失尖峰都没有出现。

e134c954a2b5.en: The step size itself should change during training. A constant rate is the simplest. <bookmark mark='a'/> A cosine schedule warms up briefly, starting with tiny steps while the weights are still random, so the first updates don't blow up. Then it glides smoothly down to zero. <bookmark mark='b'/> Warmup–stable–decay holds the rate flat for most of the run, and only drops it at the end. <bookmark mark='c'/> Here they are on the character model. While the rate stays high, the loss plateaus. When it falls, the loss drops sharply, as the noisy cloud from chapter one shrinks onto the bottom. <bookmark mark='d'/> Warmup–stable–decay is popular for a practical reason: you can stop at any point, decay briefly, and get a finished model, without knowing in advance how long you'll train.
e134c954a2b5.zh: 步长本身，在训练过程中也应该变化。恒定的学习率最简单。<bookmark mark='a'/>余弦调度先短暂地预热：权重还是随机的时候，先迈很小的步子，免得最初的几次更新就发散。然后平滑地一路降到0。<bookmark mark='b'/>预热–稳定–衰减，在大部分时间里让学习率保持不变，只在最后才把它降下来。<bookmark mark='c'/>把它们放到字符模型上看。学习率一直很高时，损失停在一个平台上。学习率一降，损失就陡然下降，因为第1章那团带噪声的云，收缩到了谷底。<bookmark mark='d'/>预热–稳定–衰减很受欢迎，原因很实际：你可以在任何时候停下来，短暂地衰减一下，就得到一个训练完成的模型，不用事先知道要训练多久。

2c28442a284d.en: Let's take stock. How you walk downhill matters as much as the hill. Small random batches make each step cheap and noisy, and the noise settles into a cloud whose size is set by the step and the batch. Training pushes the sharpness up to two over the learning rate, and lives at that edge. Momentum and Adam reshape each step, and Muon makes a matrix's step push equally in every direction. And the schedule decides when the cloud finally contracts onto a good answer.
2c28442a284d.zh: 我们来盘点一下。怎样下山，和山本身一样要紧。随机的小批量让每一步又便宜又带噪声，而噪声最终化作一团云，云有多大，由步长和批量决定。训练会把锐度推高到学习率分之2，并且就待在那道边缘上。动量和Adam重新塑造每一步，Muon则让矩阵的每一步，在每个方向上都推得一样多。而学习率调度，决定了这团云什么时候最终收缩到一个好的答案上。

76253f8142fa.en: Next, we scale up. How should the learning rate change when the model gets wider? How big should the batch be, and how long should we train? That's part twelve. And these optimizers return whenever a model in this series is actually trained.
76253f8142fa.zh: 接下来，我们要扩大规模。模型变宽时，学习率应该怎样变？批量应该多大，又该训练多久？这是第12部分的内容。而每当本系列真正训练一个模型，这些优化器都会再次登场。

3c44a6267e2b.en: Next time: the mathematics of scale. Why bigger models predictably get better, how to split a budget between parameters and data, and how to set a learning rate once and keep it as the model grows. <bookmark mark='a'/> Straight lines on log–log plots, and what they promise.
3c44a6267e2b.zh: 下一次：规模的数学。为什么模型越大越好，而且好多少是可以预测的；怎样在参数和数据之间分配预算；以及怎样只设定一次学习率，在模型变大时一直沿用。<bookmark mark='a'/>双对数坐标图上的直线，以及它们许下的承诺。

76c2acf934e6.en: Bottou, Curtis and Nocedal's survey is the best single account of stochastic optimization. Thanks for watching, and see you in part twelve.
76c2acf934e6.zh: 博图、柯蒂斯和诺塞达尔的那篇综述，是讲随机优化最好的一篇文献。感谢观看，第12部分见。

24423e78db92.en: On the same character model, with Muon on the hidden matrices, the weight grids inside the network, and AdamW on the rest: the character table, the output layer and the small bias terms. <bookmark mark='a'/> it reaches 2.51 bits, ahead of AdamW's 2.61. Muon has since been scaled up: Moonshot AI reported that it needs about half the compute of AdamW, and used a version of it to train Kimi K2.
24423e78db92.zh: 还是同一个字符模型，隐藏层的矩阵，也就是网络内部那些权重网格，用Muon；其余的用AdamW：字符表、输出层，还有那些小小的偏置项。<bookmark mark='a'/>它达到了2.51比特，领先于AdamW的2.61。此后，Muon被推广到了大得多的规模：月之暗面报告说，它只需要AdamW大约一半的算力，还用它的一个变体训练了Kimi K2。

chapters_en.Outro: Recap, and where this comes back
